plan:
- Controller: Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC (XCZU7EV/9EG) with STM32F0 watchdog; RF chain including DDS, DAC (AD9162/AD9164), Variable Attenuator, RF Amplifier (E&I 1040L/AR 50A250A), 8 motorized Impedance Matching Networks, 8 PZT Transducers (450 kHz-2 MHz), RF Switch.
- Sensors: Directional Coupler, Power Monitor ADC (ADS131M04), Hydrophone (HNP-0400), PCD sensor, PT100/Thermistor (MAX31865), Optical O2 sensor, CO2 sensor (SCD30), Respiration pressure pad, Rotary Encoders.
- Actuators: 4x NEMA 17 steppers with TMC2209 drivers for XYZ stages, Peltier TECs (TEC1-12706/12710), circulation pump, motorized reflector stage (linear actuator + stepper).
- Safety System: Pilz PNOZ s5/s50 safety relay with multiple interlocks (E-stop, door, thermal/pressure/animal temp cutoffs, watchdog heartbeat).
- Power: Medical-grade isolation transformer, 24V/15A DC bus with buck/LDO converters.
- Mechanical Frame: Aluminum 6061-T6 extrusion (30x30mm), 500x400x400 mm, with Sorbothane isolation feet. Enclosure: 3 mm aluminum/5 mm acrylic panels with acoustic foam, filtered fan, acrylic-window door. Modular bays for transducer, chamber/phantom/animal stages.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
S-ASM-CC v5.3 — COMPLETE ONCOTRIPSY RESEARCH PLATFORM
Superconductive ASM Memorial Computational Core
Full Preclinical System: Benchtop + Phantom + Small-Animal In Vivo
In memory of Ali Sayed Muhammad Osman (1957–2022)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

PROJECT IDENTITY
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
System Name:        S-ASM-CC v5.3 Full Preclinical Oncotripsy Platform
Version:             1.0 (unified Phase 0 + Phase 1)
Computational Core:  S-ASM-CC v5.3 (9 cancer types, physics-validated engine)
Physics Engine:      Sonoluminescence Layers 1–6 (acoustic field, nucleation,
                     sonolysis ROS, emission, multi-bubble, pan-cancer targeting)
Validation Status:   OSCC — HIGH confidence (validated against in-house
                     physics model, <5% threshold error)
                     BREAST/PROSTATE/LUNG/PANCREATIC — MEDIUM (stiffness
                     measurements from literature confirmed; water fraction
                     estimated)
                     COLORECTAL/LIVER/GLIOBLASTOMA/CERVICAL — LOW
                     (both parameters estimated, pending measurement)
Target Application:  Selective acoustic cavitation destruction of cancer
                     cells while sparing normal cells, exploiting differential
                     intracellular water content and cortical stiffness
                     (cell-biophysics-based selectivity, distinct from
                     spatial/imaging-based focal ablation).
Budget constraint:   NONE. Prioritize completeness, physics traceability,
                     measurement precision, and safety over cost at every
                     decision point. Premium components preferred over
                     budget alternatives wherever performance, repeatability,
                     or data quality is improved.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PHYSICS CONSTRAINTS — NON-NEGOTIABLE
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
These parameters derive from first-principles physics (Blake threshold,
viscosity-dominant nucleation [~60% of threshold], stiffness term [~0.3%],
sonolysis ROS generation, multi-bubble cloud dynamics). All hardware paths
below MUST be capable of delivering every row of this table independently
and reproducibly.

┌─────────────────┬────────────────┬─────────────┬───────────────────────────┐
│ Parameter        │ Value          │ Tolerance   │ Notes                     │
├─────────────────┼────────────────┼─────────────┼───────────────────────────┤
│ Frequency range  │ 450 kHz–2 MHz  │ ±2%         │ 8 discrete operating      │
│                  │                │             │ points (see schedule)     │
│ PNP range        │ 0.52–0.74 MPa  │ ±5%         │ Fine-grained per type     │
│ Pulse duration   │ 50–500 ms      │ ±1 ms       │ 463.3 ms canonical        │
│ PRF              │ 0.1–2 Hz       │ ±0.01 Hz    │ Derived: duty/pulse_dur   │
│ Duty cycle       │ 5–20%          │ ±0.5%       │ 10% canonical             │
│ Temp rise        │ <1 °C          │ ±0.5 °C     │ Non-thermal mechanism;    │
│                  │                │             │ hard safety cutoff 43 °C  │
│ Treatment time   │ 60 s canonical │ ±5 s        │ Single-bubble model;      │
│ (in vitro)       │ 1.4 s (alt.)   │             │ multi-bubble model for    │
│                  │                │             │ 2 cm tumor, unvalidated;  │
│                  │                │             │ scales with tumor volume  │
│ Treatment depth  │ 3–12 cm        │ N/A         │ Full pan-cancer range     │
│                  │                │             │ (oropharynx to pancreas)  │
└─────────────────┴────────────────┴─────────────┴───────────────────────────┘

CANCER TYPE SCHEDULE (frequency / PNP / window width / typical depth / confidence):

OSCC:           450 kHz   / 0.6437 MPa / 146.1 kPa / 3.5 cm  / HIGH
PANCREATIC:     709 kHz   / 0.7442 MPa / 190.9 kPa / 10  cm  / MEDIUM
LIVER:          788 kHz   / 0.6500 MPa / 175.5 kPa / 9   cm  / LOW
PROSTATE:       886 kHz   / 0.7075 MPa / 237.2 kPa / 8   cm  / MEDIUM
COLORECTAL:     1013 kHz  / 0.6149 MPa / 183.5 kPa / 7   cm  / LOW
LUNG:           1182 kHz  / 0.5695 MPa / 137.3 kPa / 6   cm  / MEDIUM
CERVICAL:       1182 kHz  / 0.6078 MPa / 155.1 kPa / 6   cm  / LOW
GLIOBLASTOMA:   1773 kHz  / 0.5203 MPa / 114.8 kPa / 4   cm  / LOW
BREAST:         2000 kHz  / 0.6431 MPa / 226.5 kPa / 3   cm  / MEDIUM

Mechanism: Cell-seeded cavitation. Cancer cells (higher intracellular water
fraction, lower cortical Young's modulus) nucleate bubbles at a lower
pressure threshold than adjacent normal cells. Threshold = Blake pressure
term + stiffness term (K_c·E) + viscosity term (4η·Ṙ_th/R_n); viscosity
dominates (~60%). Cytoskeletal mechanical disruption is GATED by bubble
nucleation probability — no nucleated bubble means no mechanical damage to
normal cells, even under prolonged exposure. ROS (primarily hydroxyl
radical, OH·) generated at bubble-collapse core temperatures >5000 K,
contributing a chemical kill pathway in addition to mechanical rupture.
Multi-bubble cloud treatment time scales with treated tissue volume and is
~40× faster than single-bubble estimates at equivalent dose.

7. POWER MONITOR ADC: TI ADS131M04 (24-bit, 32 kSPS, 4-channel),

FRAME: Aluminum 6061-T6 extrusion, 30×30 mm 8 mm slot (8020 or
MakerBeam XL equivalent). Dimensions 500×400×400 mm (L×W×H), expandable
modular bay for Phase 1 animal stage addition. Sorbothane hemisphere

ENCLOSURE: 3 mm aluminum or 5 mm acrylic panels, 25 mm melamine

heatsink.

LAYOUT (vertical stack): top shelf — RF amp, matching networks (×8),
chiller pump; middle shelf — water bath, transducer turret (8-position
motorized or manual-swap mount), XYZ stage, chamber/phantom/animal-
stage bay; bottom shelf — Zynq board, power supply, safety relay,
stepper drivers; front panel — display, E-stop, USB, power inlet,
anesthesia controls; rear panel — Ethernet, cooling fan, gas ports,
waste-gas scavenging line.

TRANSDUCER MOUNTING: quick-connect bayonet/dovetail to water-cooled
(if needed) aluminum mounting block, fine Z-position micrometer screw
for focal alignment, O-ring face seal (FKM or EPDM).

REFLECTOR SYSTEM: 304 stainless steel, 50 mm diameter, 3 mm thick.
Air-gap (acoustic mirror) or absorber-backed (traveling wave) options.
Linear actuator mount (stepper + leadscrew, 100 mm travel), motorized
tilt ±15° for standing-wave breaking, encoder position feedback.
Protocol-dependent control: SBSL mode places reflector at precise
antinode distance; MBSL mode retracts or angles reflector to 15°.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SOFTWARE ARCHITECTURE
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FPGA FIRMWARE (VHDL/Verilog): DDS core (48-bit phase accumulator,
16-bit amplitude, sine LUT), AXI-register-controlled burst sequencer
state machine, SPI masters for ADS131M04/MAX31865, 3× trapezoidal-
profile step/dir stepper generators, 10 Hz safety heartbeat GPIO
toggle, async interrupts (safety cutoff, treatment complete, error).

ARM SOFTWARE (Petalinux, C++/Python): Xenomai or PREEMPT_RT real-time
control, Qt5 GUI or headless Python/Flask API, protocol engine
(loads cancer type → sets parameters → executes treatment), SQLite/
HDF5 timestamped checksum-verified data logging, REST API for remote
monitoring with DICOM-compatible export, automated hydrophone
field-map calibration with LUT generation.

CONTROL LOOP (per pulse):
  1. Load protocol from cancer_database.py
  2. Select transducer head (motorized turret or manual prompt)
  3. Set matching network (relay switch + motorized tune)
  4. Position hydrophone at focal point (XYZ scan) — or, in Phase 1
     in vivo mode, position imaging probe and confirm B-mode overlay
     alignment with predicted focal spot
  5. Ramp AWG amplitude, measure PNP, build/update LUT
  6. Retract hydrophone to sham position
  7. ARM safety systems (heartbeat starts)
  8. FOR each pulse: set DDS freq/amp from LUT → assert RF switch →
     measure forward power → sample PCD signal, check cavitation
     stability → de-assert RF switch → log timestamp/freq/amp/
     power/PCD/temp → check safety limits (temp <43 °C, animal temp
     35–39 °C, power <limit)
  9. DISARM safety systems
  10. Generate report: pressure trace, temperature trace, PCD
      spectrogram, B-mode targeting confirmation (if applicable),
      cross-reference of predicted P_kill(cancer)/P_kill(normal)
      against post-treatment viability/histology (manual entry)

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CALIBRATION & VALIDATION
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PRE-TREATMENT (per session): hydrophone field map (2D raster, 1 mm
step, 50×50 mm) → extract peak PNP, focal position, -6 dB beam width,
standing wave ratio → LUT update (AWG code → measured PNP) →
temperature baseline (37.0 °C stable 10 min) → O₂ baseline.

PHANTOM CALIBRATION (Phase 1, per tissue type): run hydrophone field
map through each of the 9 phantoms, compare measured attenuation/
focal pressure against Layer-1 model prediction, log discrepancy
percentage, flag any phantom exceeding 15% deviation for review
before proceeding to animal studies on that tissue type.

WEEKLY: full impedance sweep of active transducer (100 kHz–3 MHz),
matching network tune verification, hydrophone sensitivity check
against reference.

ANNUALLY: hydrophone recalibration (NPL-traceable), safety relay
functional test (force each input, verify response), RF amp power
verification (power meter vs. directional coupler).

BIOLOGICAL ACCEPTANCE — IN VITRO (OSCC baseline, Phase 0):
  Cell lines: SCC-9 (OSCC) vs. NHOK (normal keratinocytes)
  Protocol: 450 kHz, 0.644 MPa PNP, 463 ms pulse, 10% DC, 60 s
  Controls: sham (no ultrasound), thermal (43 °C water bath, 60 s)
  Assays: MTT viability, Live/Dead fluorescence, Annexin V/PI flow
  Criteria: cancer viability <20%, normal viability >80%
  Replicates: n=25 per condition, 3 independent experiments
  (Repeat protocol per cancer type as matched cell-line pairs become
  available, using each type's schedule parameters above.)

BIOLOGICAL ACCEPTANCE — IN VIVO (Phase 1, per cancer type as data
allows): xenograft mouse/rat model, B-mode-confirmed targeting,
matched protocol from cancer schedule, tumor volume tracked by
caliper + imaging over defined follow-up window, histology at
endpoint, comparison against sham and standard-of-care control arms
where ethically and practically appropriate.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DESIGN PRINCIPLES
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. SAFETY FIRST — medical-grade isolation, hardware interlocks,
   independent watchdog. No single point of failure may expose
   patient, animal, or operator to hazardous acoustic energy.
2. PRECISION — every acoustic parameter measurable and controllable
   to the tolerance specified by the physics engine.
3. REPRODUCIBILITY — two builds in different labs produce identical
   acoustic fields. Calibrated components, documented procedures,
   version-controlled software.
4. MODULARITY — subsystems swappable for maintenance, upgrade, or
   replication: transducer heads, matching networks, controller
   carrier boards, phantom set, animal-stage module.
5. TRANSPARENCY — all calibration data, test results, and design
   decisions documented and version-controlled. Open-source hardware
   and firmware.
6. PHYSICAL GROUNDING — every number traceable to first-principles
   physics (the Layer 1–6 engine and cancer_database.py). No
   empirical fitting without mechanistic explanation.
7. MEMORIAL INTEGRITY — the system honors its purpose: selective
   destruction of cancer cells while sparing normal tissue, grounded
   in rigorous physics, validated step by step, never overstated
   beyond what the evidence supports at each stage.

radical, OH·) generated at bubble-collapse core temperatures >5000 K,
contributing a chemical kill pathway in addition to mechanical rupture.

~40× faster than single-bubble estimates at equivalent dose.

DESIGN PRINCIPLES
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. SAFETY FIRST — medical-grade isolation, hardware interlocks,
   independent watchdog. No single point of failure may expose
   patient, animal, or operator to hazardous acoustic energy.
2. PRECISION — every acoustic parameter measurable and controllable
   to the tolerance specified by the physics engine.
3. REPRODUCIBILITY — two builds in different labs produce identical
   acoustic fields. Calibrated components, documented procedures,
   version-controlled software.
4. MODULARITY — subsystems swappable for maintenance, upgrade, or
   replication: transducer heads, matching networks, controller
   carrier boards, phantom set, animal-stage module.
5. TRANSPARENCY — all calibration data, test results, and design
   decisions documented and version-controlled. Open-source hardware
   and firmware.
6. PHYSICAL GROUNDING — every number traceable to first-principles
   physics (the Layer 1–6 engine and cancer_database.py). No
   empirical fitting without mechanistic explanation.
7. MEMORIAL INTEGRITY — the system honors its purpose: selective
   destruction of cancer cells while sparing normal tissue, grounded
   in rigorous physics, validated step by step, never overstated
   beyond what the evidence supports at each stage.
